n: int; number of vertices N (a count, unitless), n ≥ 1. Vertices are numbered 0, 1, …, n-1 (0-based indices); the number of rows of dist and the number of columns in each row must both equal n.
p: int; number of medians (facilities) that must be selected exactly (a count, unitless), 1 ≤ p ≤ n; trivial cases such as n = 1 or p = n are valid.
dist: list[list[float | null]]; n×n precomputed shortest-path distance matrix; the outer list has length n, each row has length n, indices are 0-based. dist[i][j] is the shortest-path distance from vertex i to vertex j: the first dimension (row) i is the origin, i.e., the vertex being served; the second dimension (column) j is the destination, i.e., the candidate median. Finite values are non-negative reals (writing them as integers such as 3 is equally valid); negative values do not occur; the unit is not given in the problem statement, and the objective value has the same unit. null means j is unreachable from i (+∞) and is the only unreachability marker; any numeric value, however large, denotes a reachable distance; no big-number sentinel is used. The matrix need not be symmetric: dist[i][j] may differ from dist[j][i]; always use the direction dist[i][j] (vertex i to median j). Guarantees: dist[i][i] = 0 for all i; the triangle inequality dist[i][k] ≤ dist[i][j] + dist[j][k] holds for all i, j, k (a null term is treated as +∞); there exists at least one choice of exactly p distinct medians such that every vertex i has some selected median j with dist[i][j] not null.
